final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is substantively correct in one respect: rollout controls, rollback capability, and a 6% launch posture are deployment mitigations, not proof that the disclosure predicate was satisfied. But that clarification does not cure the core audit gap. Under the policy text, rollout controls mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable; the available record says neither condition is met. The Actor's proposed caveated certification also remains under-supported because there is still no admissible evidence that the required model-card limitation was actually documented in an approved record and that such disclosure is sufficient under the governing certification criterion despite continued exposure. So this is not clean compliance, and it is not yet supported even as compliant_with_caveats on the present record.
remaining_concerns: The affected utility arrears assistance segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The policy predicate for using rollout controls as mitigation is still unmet because the use case is not excluded and there is no reviewed, approved risk acceptance covering that exposure.
There is still no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure was actually completed, reviewed, and approved.
The Actor's narrowed position is more precise, but it is still conditional on documentation that is argued for rather than evidenced.
